placement.position_note: Interpretive placement on a GENERATED lot, not a recovered parcel. The lot geometry is the K7 plat module's — this project has never read Thompson's numbering off a sheet, and the side lot lines and the alley are conjectural even where the block face is not. The building stands 5.0 m back from its street edge, which is a typology for the period and not a measurement of this lot. The whole footprint — not its centre — is tested against the platted street corridors, against its own lot lines and against every other footprint in the dataset, so no invented building of this parcel stands in the roadway; clearing the roadway is not the same as standing on a recovered lot.

siding_exposure_m.note: INVENTED WITHIN A STOCK SET, NOT DERIVED. No source states the exposed face of any Chicago building's siding. The value is one of four period mill sidings — 4.5, 5, 5.5 or 6 in to the weather; this roof wears 6 in — dealt in this building's own parcel recipe: drawn on this record's stable key from the stocks its household class may hang (5 in, 5.5 in or 6 in; T-1839, docs/LIBERTIES.md L352), then advanced within them so that no roof of the parcel standing within 60 m hangs the same course. It is NOT keyed to a construction season the way the named buildings' stocks are: this record's 1835-01-01 is the programme's count-unit convention and not a date anything was built, so keying to it would deal every anonymous roof in the town one stock. The separation is the surface variety T-0049 reconstructs, not a claim about 1835. docs/LIBERTIES.md L148 owns the invention and the recipe half is recorded beside it, under `tools/siding_stock.py`.

persons.name: No Sha Cum
persons.note: CARDED FROM THE BORDERLINE ROSTER'S R6 (T-1376, stage `underdocumented`). Enrolled at Chicago in 1832 in the company the Black Hawk War roll heads INDIAN, with no 1835 corroboration and no card. The licence is R3's — the same roll, the same year, the same page — and the twenty men of Kercheval's company the town already carries were re-admitted under it. The roll prints him as `NO SHA CUM`, company `INDIAN`, enrolled at `CHICAGO`. The research READ this name and WITHHELD it, and that refusal is not overturned: this record is a reconstruction of what the town looks like if the name is admitted at the limit of its own evidence, and it says so on its face. The reading, the source and the refusal stand at `civic:data/research/civic/records/blackhawk_war_1832_chicago.json#records/blackhawk_1832_079#0` in data/reconstruction/1835_borderline_roster.json. REVIEW REQUIRED: this card is a record of a Native person at Chicago in the three years of the removal, and AGENTS.md's standing constraint holds it for review by Native scholars or community organisations before any scene carrying it may be marked released. No figure is drawn (L1).

citations.citation: Chicago · July 1835: Building Inventory and Architectural Reconstruction Specification. Prepared for Kevin Haas, August 2026.
what_it_supplies: A 665-roof production target with independently reconcilable group, district, level, and construction totals.
Thirty-five architectural family definitions with dimensional and massing bands.
District character, spacing, variation, finish, and chronology constraints for a July 1835 reconstruction.
A required distinction between named documentary landmarks and anonymous inferred infill.
what_it_does_not_supply: A surviving July 1835 building census or parcel-by-parcel roof register.
Exact locations, dimensions, appearance, occupants, or construction dates for anonymous roofs.
Authority to replace stronger building-specific evidence already represented in the dataset.
